title: CHORDONOMICON: A Dataset of 666,000 Songs and their Chord Progressions
abstract: arXiv:2410.22046v4 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Chord progressions encapsulate important information about music, pertaining to its structure and conveyed emotions. They serve as the backbone of musical composition, and in many cases, they are the sole information required for a musician to play along and follow the music. Despite their importance, chord progressions as a data domain remain underexplored; existing datasets lack the scale, structural annotation, and metadata diversity required for rigorous evaluation of music understanding models. In this work, we present Chordonomicon, the largest dataset of its kind, containing over 666,000 song-level symbolic chord progressions, annotated with structural parts (verse, chorus, bridge, etc.), genre, and release date, created by scraping various sources of user-generated progressions and associated metadata, showing strong similarity to well-established prior datasets. translated_title: CHORDONOMICON：包含666,000首歌曲及其和弦进行的数据集
translated_abstract: 和弦进行蕴含着关于音乐的重要信息，涉及音乐的结构及其所传达的情感。它们是音乐创作的支柱，在许多情况下，也是音乐人进行演奏和跟随音乐所需的唯一信息。尽管和弦进行如此重要，但作为一个数据领域，它仍未得到充分探索；现有数据集缺乏对音乐理解模型进行严格评估所需的规模、结构标注和元数据多样性。在本研究中，我们提出了Chordonomicon，这是目前此类数据集中规模最大的一个，包含超过666,000首歌曲级别的符号化和弦进行，并标注了结构部分（主歌、副歌、桥段等）、流派和发行日期。该数据集通过抓取多种用户生成的和弦进行及相关元数据来源构建而成，并与已有的知名数据集表现出高度相似性。除数据集本身之外，我们还提出了一个可复现的基准（测试）……
tldr: 提出了目前规模最大的和弦进行数据集Chordonomicon，包含超过666,000首歌曲的和弦进行，并附带结构段落、流派和发行日期等标注，为音乐理解模型的严格评估提供了可复现的基准。
en_tdlr: We present Chordonomicon, the largest chord progression dataset to date, containing over 666,000 songs annotated with structural parts, genre, and release date, providing a reproducible benchmark for rigorous evaluation of music understanding models.
